title: Unit 1 Mixed Review Core Test
description: Review rigid transformations, congruence, parallel-line angle relationships, triangle angles, and exterior angles.

questions.questionText: Point A(3, -2) is translated 5 units left and 4 units up. What is A'?
questions.explanation: Move left by subtracting 5 from x and move up by adding 4 to y: (3 - 5, -2 + 4) = (-2, 2).

questions.questionText: Point B(-4, 7) is reflected across the x-axis. What is B'?
questions.explanation: A reflection across the x-axis keeps x the same and changes the sign of y.

questions.questionText: Point C(6, -1) is reflected across the y-axis. What is C'?
questions.explanation: A reflection across the y-axis changes the sign of x and keeps y the same.

questions.questionText: Point D(2, 5) is rotated 180 degrees about the origin. What is D'?
questions.explanation: A 180 degree rotation about the origin sends (x, y) to (-x, -y).

questions.questionText: Which transformation always preserves side lengths and angle measures?
questions.explanation: A rotation is a rigid transformation, so it preserves lengths and angle measures.

questions.questionText: Two figures are congruent. Which statement must be true?
options: Corresponding side lengths and angle measures are equal.
The figures must be in the same location.
questions.correctAnswer: Corresponding side lengths and angle measures are equal.
questions.explanation: Congruent figures have matching side lengths and matching angle measures.

questions.questionText: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 64 degrees. Its corresponding angle is what?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel.

questions.questionText: A triangle has angles of 42 degrees and 73 degrees. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: Triangle angles add to 180 degrees: 180 - 42 - 73 = 65.

questions.questionText: A triangle has remote interior angles of 51 degrees and 68 degrees. What is the exterior angle?
questions.explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 51 + 68 = 119.

questions.questionText: Which transformation is not rigid?
questions.explanation: A dilation changes size unless the scale factor is 1, so it is not generally rigid.

questions.questionText: Point P(-3, 4) is translated by (6, -5), then reflected across the y-axis. What is the final image?
questions.explanation: Translate first: (-3 + 6, 4 - 5) = (3, -1). Reflect across the y-axis to get (-3, -1).

questions.questionText: Point Q(2, -7) is reflected across the x-axis, then rotated 180 degrees about the origin. What is the final image?
questions.explanation: Reflect across the x-axis: (2, 7). Rotate 180 degrees: (-2, -7).

questions.questionText: A point is translated from (5, -3) to (-2, 6). What translation was used?
questions.explanation: The x-coordinate changes by -7 and the y-coordinate changes by +9.

questions.questionText: Point R(-6, 2) is rotated 90 degrees clockwise about the origin. What is R'?
questions.explanation: A 90 degree clockwise rotation sends (x, y) to (y, -x).

questions.questionText: Point S(-1, 5) is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. What is S'?
questions.explanation: A 90 degree counterclockwise rotation sends (x, y) to (-y, x).

questions.questionText: Triangle ABC has side lengths 5, 8, and 10. Triangle DEF has side lengths 5, 8, and 11. Are the triangles congruent?
options: Yes, because two side lengths match.
Yes, because all triangles are congruent after a translation.
No, because congruent figures must face the same way.
No, because one corresponding side length is different.
questions.correctAnswer: No, because one corresponding side length is different.
questions.explanation: Congruent triangles need all corresponding side lengths and angle measures to match.

questions.questionText: A figure is reflected across the y-axis and then translated 4 units right. Which property is preserved?
questions.explanation: Both reflection and translation are rigid transformations, so area is preserved.

questions.questionText: Two same-side interior angles formed by parallel lines are 7x degrees and 5x degrees. What is x?
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles are supplementary: 7x + 5x = 180, so x = 15.

questions.questionText: Two alternate interior angles are 3x + 8 degrees and 5x - 20 degrees. What is x?
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal: 3x + 8 = 5x - 20, so x = 14.

questions.questionText: A triangle has angles x degrees, x + 20 degrees, and 70 degrees. What is x?
A right triangle has acute angles 2x + 6 degrees and x + 24 degrees. What is x?
questions.explanation: The acute angles add to 90: 2x + 6 + x + 24 = 90, so x = 20.

questions.questionText: A triangle has an exterior angle of 128 degrees and one remote interior angle of 47 degrees. What is the other remote interior angle?
questions.explanation: The remote interior angles add to the exterior angle, so 128 - 47 = 81.

questions.questionText: An exterior angle is 4x + 6 degrees. Its remote interior angles are 2x + 10 degrees and 56 degrees. What is x?
A triangle has adjacent interior angle 74 degrees. Its remote interior angles are 39 degrees and y degrees. What is y?
questions.explanation: The exterior angle is 180 - 74 = 106. Then y = 106 - 39 = 67.

questions.questionText: Which sequence maps (1, 2) to (-3, 6)?
options: translate 4 units left and 4 units up
translate 2 units right and 8 units up
questions.correctAnswer: translate 4 units left and 4 units up
questions.explanation: From (1, 2) to (-3, 6), x changes by -4 and y changes by +4.

questions.questionText: A quadrilateral is translated, reflected, and rotated. What can you conclude about the image?
options: It is congruent to the original quadrilateral.
It must be similar but not congruent.
It must return to the same location.
questions.correctAnswer: It is congruent to the original quadrilateral.
questions.explanation: Translations, reflections, and rotations are all rigid transformations.

questions.questionText: A triangle has angle ratio 2:3:4. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: There are 9 parts, so each part is 20 degrees. The largest angle is 4 parts, or 80 degrees.

questions.questionText: Remote interior angles are in the ratio 3:5, and the exterior angle is 144 degrees. What is the larger remote interior angle?
questions.explanation: The ratio has 8 parts. Each part is 18 degrees, so the larger angle is 5 x 18 = 90 degrees.

questions.questionText: A figure has vertices A(0, 1), B(3, 1), and C(0, 5). After a translation, A' is (4, -2). What is C'?
questions.explanation: The translation is 4 right and 3 down. Apply it to C(0, 5) to get (4, 2).

questions.questionText: A triangle has two angles of 58 degrees and 58 degrees. What type of triangle is it by sides?
questions.explanation: Two equal angles mean the opposite sides are equal, so the triangle is isosceles.

questions.questionText: A line pair is cut by a transversal. Corresponding angles measure 82 degrees and 82 degrees. What can you conclude?
options: The lines could be parallel because corresponding angles are equal.
The angles must be same-side interior.
questions.correctAnswer: The lines could be parallel because corresponding angles are equal.
questions.explanation: Equal corresponding angles are evidence that the crossed lines are parallel.

questions.questionText: A point (a, b) is reflected across the x-axis. Which rule describes the image?
questions.explanation: Reflecting across the x-axis changes only the sign of the y-coordinate.

questions.questionText: A point (a, b) is rotated 180 degrees about the origin. Which rule describes the image?
questions.explanation: A 180 degree rotation changes the signs of both coordinates.

questions.questionText: A triangle has angles 5x - 5 degrees, 3x + 10 degrees, and 95 degrees. What is x?
An interior angle and exterior angle form a linear pair. The exterior angle is 3x degrees and the interior angle is 2x + 30 degrees. What is x?
Point T(-2, 3) is reflected across the y-axis, translated 5 units down, then rotated 180 degrees about the origin. What is the final image?
questions.explanation: Reflect to (2, 3), translate to (2, -2), then rotate 180 degrees to (-2, 2).

questions.questionText: A student says a reflection and translation cannot prove congruence because the figure changes location. What is the best response?
options: The student is correct because only rotations prove congruence.
Location can change; rigid transformations preserve size and shape.
The figures are congruent only if labels disappear.
questions.correctAnswer: Location can change; rigid transformations preserve size and shape.
questions.explanation: Congruence depends on preserved side lengths and angle measures, not staying in the same place.

questions.questionText: Two same-side interior angles are 4x + 17 degrees and 3x + 23 degrees. What is the larger angle?
questions.explanation: They add to 180: 7x + 40 = 180, so x = 20. The angles are 97 and 83 degrees.

questions.questionText: An exterior angle is 5x - 4 degrees. Its remote interior angles are 2x + 9 degrees and x + 35 degrees. What is x?
A triangle has angles 2x + 10 degrees, 3x - 5 degrees, and 4x + 4 degrees. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: The sum is 9x + 9 = 180, so x = 19. The angles are 48, 52, and 80 degrees, so the largest is 80 degrees.

questions.questionText: A triangle has exterior angle 126 degrees. One remote angle equals the adjacent interior angle. The other remote angle is 72 degrees. What is the equal angle?
questions.explanation: The adjacent interior angle is 180 - 126 = 54 degrees. The other remote angle is 126 - 72 = 54 degrees.

questions.questionText: A sequence maps A(1, -4) to A'(-4, -1). Which single transformation does this?
options: rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin
translate 5 units left and 3 units down
rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin
questions.correctAnswer: rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin
questions.explanation: A 90 degree clockwise rotation sends (x, y) to (y, -x). For (1, -4), that gives (-4, -1).

questions.questionText: A quadrilateral has vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), (4, 3), and (0, 3). Which transformed image is definitely congruent?
questions.explanation: The correct image is a translation 2 right and 1 down, preserving side lengths 4 and 3.

questions.questionText: A student claims two figures are congruent because their corresponding angles are equal. What is missing?
options: Evidence that the figures have different areas.
Evidence that corresponding side lengths are also equal.
Evidence that one figure is larger.
Evidence that labels are in alphabetical order.
questions.correctAnswer: Evidence that corresponding side lengths are also equal.
questions.explanation: Equal angles alone can show similarity, but congruence also needs matching side lengths.

questions.questionText: A triangle has remote interior angles x + 18 degrees and 2x - 6 degrees. Its adjacent interior angle is 72 degrees. What is x?
questions.explanation: The exterior angle is 108 degrees. x + 18 + 2x - 6 = 108, so 3x + 12 = 108 and x = 32.

questions.questionText: Two alternate exterior angles are 6x - 11 degrees and 4x + 21 degrees. What is x?
questions.explanation: Alternate exterior angles are equal: 6x - 11 = 4x + 21, so x = 16.

questions.questionText: A point is rotated 90 degrees clockwise, then reflected across the x-axis. What is the rule for (x, y)?
questions.explanation: Clockwise rotation sends (x, y) to (y, -x). Reflecting across the x-axis changes the y-coordinate sign, giving (y, x).

questions.questionText: A student solves 48 + 67 + e = 180 to find an exterior angle. What should the equation be?
questions.explanation: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

questions.questionText: Triangle A'B'C' is produced from triangle ABC by a rotation and reflection. Which statement is strongest evidence of congruence?
options: The image is farther from the origin.
Every corresponding side and angle matches after the rigid transformations.
questions.correctAnswer: Every corresponding side and angle matches after the rigid transformations.
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations preserve all side lengths and angle measures, which is enough for congruence.

questions.questionText: A triangle has angles in the ratio 3:4:5. One side is extended at the largest angle. What is that exterior angle?
questions.explanation: The angle ratio has 12 parts, so each part is 15 degrees. The largest interior angle is 75 degrees, and its adjacent exterior angle is 180 - 75 = 105 degrees.
